claims.claim: Global flag --env / -e, default empty string, resolves to `default`
`--config` default is `config.arena.yaml`, or `arena.yaml` when only that exists
Global flag --pack, optional pre-compiled .pack.json, default compiles from --config
The three flags are persistent: valid on every deploy subcommand incl. adapter and config
When --pack is omitted the CLI compiles the pack from --config on the fly
With --pack the CLI reads that .pack.json instead of compiling
Synopsis: promptarena deploy [subcommand] [flags]
deploy manages prompt pack deployments through adapter plugins; supports plan, apply, status, destroy
Bare `deploy` runs plan and apply sequentially and is the default command
deploy process step 1-2: load arena.yaml deploy config and resolve pack (compile or --pack)
deploy process step 3: merge base config with environment overrides
deploy process steps 4-5: load prior state, refresh it from the live environment before planning
deploy process steps 6-7: call adapter Plan then adapter Apply
deploy process step 8: save state with adapter state, pack checksum and timestamps
deploy plan previews changes without modifying any resources
The first plan line is `Deploy plan for environment: <env> (provider: <provider>)`, followed by an `  Adapter:` line
plan output shows a `Changes:` header, rows like `  + agent_runtime.greeting    Create agent runtime`, and a `Summary: 1 to create, ...` line
Change symbols: + CREATE, ~ UPDATE, - DELETE, ! DRIFT, space NO_CHANGE
Unchanged resources are shown in plan output as a row with a space symbol
deploy apply is called automatically by deploy
deploy apply [flags] applies deployment changes
deploy status shows current deployment status and resource health
Status output: `Status: deployed`, resource rows, then `Last deployed:`, `Pack version:` (when recorded) and `Pack checksum:`
Resource rows read `agent_runtime.greeting: healthy` and append ` — detail` when present
Status values: deployed, not_deployed, degraded, unknown
Resource health values: healthy, unhealthy, missing
With no state for the environment, `status` prints a notice and exits 0
deploy destroy tears down all managed resources
destroy step 2: with no state, print notice and exit 0
destroy step 2: call adapter Destroy with prior state
destroy step 4: delete the environment's state file and saved plan
destroy step 4: display completion message
destroy with no state prints a notice and exits 0
deploy refresh queries the adapter and updates local state to match reality; detects drift
refresh step 1: acquire deploy lock
refresh step 2: load the environment's state; with none print notice and exit 0
refresh step 3: call adapter Status with prior state
refresh step 4: update adapter state and last_refreshed timestamp
refresh step 6: display resource status with drift shown by `!`
refresh with no state prints a notice and exits 0
deploy import <type> <name> <id> takes exactly three positional arguments
Arguments: type (e.g. agent_runtime, a2a_endpoint), name (assigned in local state), id (provider-specific identifier)
Example `promptarena deploy import agent_runtime my-agent container-abc123` and `--env production` variant
import step 1: acquire deploy lock
import step 2: load prior state or create new state if none exists
import step 3: call adapter Import with resource type, name and identifier
import step 5: save updated state with last_refreshed timestamp
import step 6: display imported resource information
deploy login is available only for adapters that advertise the `login` capability
deploy login has a --provider flag; defaults to deploy.provider in the config
login step 1-2: resolve provider, connect adapter, verify login capability
login step 3: loopback callback server on 127.0.0.1 and open browser to the authorize URL with a CSRF state
login step 4: provider authenticates the user (brokers OIDC; CLI never sees the identity provider) and redirects back with a one-time code
login step 5: exchange the code via the adapter for a deploy profile and a scoped token
login step 6: merge profile into the arena config and store token in ~/.promptarena/credentials, never in arena.yaml
At deploy time the stored token is loaded automatically when the config carries no api_token
Token precedence: explicit api_token > provider env var > credentials store
deploy login needs a local browser; not for CI
deploy config import <profile-file|-> merges an exported deploy profile into the deploy config and validates it
The profile is a JSON or YAML mapping
The merge only touches deploy.config; comments, key order and other sections are preserved
`-` as the argument reads the profile from stdin
Flag --provider default `omnia`: provider to set when the deploy section is created
Flag --skip-validate default false skips validating the merged config against the adapter
config import step 2: deep-merge under spec.deploy.config, creating the deploy section with provider if absent; existing keys overridden, nested mappings merged
config import step 3: write the config back; the file must already exist and its permission bits are preserved
config import step 4: unless --skip-validate, validate via the adapter's validate_config RPC
deploy adapter install <provider>[@<version>] installs an adapter binary from the registry
install step 1: look up provider in the built-in adapter registry, which supplies its GitHub repo
install step 2: version is the pinned one, otherwise the newest release from the GitHub Releases API
install step 3: download binary from GitHub Releases for current OS/architecture
install step 4: installed to ~/.promptarena/adapters/promptarena-deploy-{provider}
install step 5: executable permissions 0755
A newly released adapter is installable immediately without rebuilding PromptArena (version resolved live)
If the GitHub API is unreachable, install falls back to the registry's recorded version and warns
Fallback warning text: `warning: could not resolve latest agentcore from GitHub (...); falling back to registry default v0.3.1`
The recorded registry version is refreshed daily and only affects the offline path
Download URL: https://github.com/{repo}/releases/download/v{version}/promptarena-deploy-{provider}_{os}_{arch}
deploy adapter list lists installed adapters
list output: each search directory with adapters printed as `label (path):` header followed by binary filenames, indented two spaces
With no adapters it prints `No adapters installed.` and a hint to run `promptarena deploy adapter install <provider>`
list search locations: 1. project-local .promptarena/adapters/, 2. user-level ~/.promptarena/adapters/
deploy adapter remove <provider> removes an installed adapter
remove deletes the binary from ~/.promptarena/adapters/
Config example: deploy.provider (required), deploy.config (optional base provider config), deploy.environments.<env>.config (per-environment overrides)
Environment config is merged with the base config; environment value wins
`config.arena.yaml` is the default config file (`arena.yaml` when only that exists)
`.promptarena/envs/<env>/deploy.state` holds the environment's deployment state (JSON)
`.promptarena/envs/<env>/deploy.lock` prevents concurrent access; kept after use
Project-local adapters at .promptarena/adapters/
User-level adapters at ~/.promptarena/adapters/
See Also links to /arena/how-to/deploy/configure/, /arena/how-to/deploy/plan-and-apply/, /arena/reference/deploy/protocol/
Subcommands present: plan, apply, status, destroy, refresh, import, login, config import, adapter install/list/remove
Plan rows use resource types such as agent_runtime and a2a_endpoint
refresh step 6: print `  Status: <status>` and each resource as `  <type>.<name>: <status>[ — <detail>]`, then `State refreshed successfully.`
Token precedence: explicit `api_token`, then the credentials store, then the provider env var
`deploy login` takes the global flags; `--config` selects the file login writes into
